1:1.headline: Kohelet comes from "gather": what exactly did he gather?
1:1.body: Rashi says Solomon gathered much wisdom, or that he spoke before a gathered crowd. Ibn Ezra says wisdom was gathered in him. Metzudat Zion says he gathered clashing views to test which was right.

sources.quote: קֹהֶלֶת. עַל־שֵׁם שֶׁקִּהֵל חָכְמוֹת הַרְבֵּה, וְכֵן בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר קוֹרֵהוּ אָגוּר בִּן־יָקֵה, שֶׁאָגַר כָּל־הַחָכְמָה וַהֲקִיאָהּ וְיֵשׁ אוֹמְרִים שֶׁהָיָה אוֹמֵר כָּל־דְבָרָיו בְהַקְהֵל
sources.says: Rashi says the name is because he gathered much wisdom, that elsewhere he is called Agur son of Yakeh, who gathered all wisdom and spat it out, and that some say he spoke all his words before a gathering.

sources.quote: וקהלת הוא שלמה כי לא היה מבני דוד משיח מלך רק הוא לבדו ונקרא כן על לשון החכמה שנקהלה בו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says Kohelet is Solomon, since he alone of David's sons was a king, and he was called that because wisdom was gathered in him.

sources.quote: קהלת. הוא ענין קבוץ ואסיפה כמו קהלת יעקב (דברים לג ד), והמלך שלמה היה נקרא כן, על שהקהיל הדעות המנגדות לצרף וללבן הצודק מהבלתי צודק
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means gathering, like "the congregation of Jacob", and Solomon was called so because he gathered opposing views to test and sort the right from the wrong.

1:2.headline: Why "vanity of vanities"? Two answers: intensity, and seven days
1:2.body: Ibn Ezra says a singular joined to a plural makes the word stronger, like "king of kings". Rashi says the seven vanities match the seven days of creation.

sources.quote: וסמיכת היחיד לרבים בעניין אחד על שני דרכים לגדולה כמו מלך מלכים ולהפך כמו עבד עבדים והבל הבלים כמוהו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says joining a singular to a plural can mean greatness, like "king of kings", or the reverse, like "servant of servants", and "hevel of havalim" is like these.

sources.quote: שִׁבְעַת הֲבָלִים כְּנֶגֶד מַעֲשֵׂה שִׁבְעַת יְמֵי בְרֵאשִׁית
sources.says: Rashi says the seven vanities correspond to the work of the seven days of creation.

1:3.headline: "Under the sun": Rashi reads it as "in exchange for Torah"
1:3.body: Rashi reads תחת as "in exchange for" and the sun as the light of the Torah, so the question is what reward there is in any toil that replaces Torah study. Ibn Ezra reads "under the sun" as the changing times the sun makes, and Metzudat David as this world.

sources.quote: תַּחַת הַשָּׁמֶשׁ. תְּמוּרַת הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁהִיא קְרוּיָה אוֹר, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר "וְתוֹרָה אוֹר", כָּל־עָמָל שֶׁהוּא מַחֲלִיף בּוֹ אֶת־עֵסֶק הַתּוֹרָה, מַה־שָׂכָר בּוֹ?
sources.says: Rashi says "under the sun" means in exchange for the Torah, which is called light, so what reward is there in any toil that replaces Torah study.

sources.quote: וענין תחת השמש הוא הזמן המתהפך כי השמש לבדו יוליד הזמן
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says "under the sun" means the turning of time, since the sun alone produces time.

sources.quote: או תחת השמש רוצה לומר בזה העולם במקום זריחת השמש
sources.says: Metzudat David says "under the sun" can mean this world, the place where the sun rises.

1:4.headline: Rashi reads "the earth" as the humble and the righteous
1:4.body: Plainly the earth stands forever. Rashi asks who truly lasts, and answers: the humble, who bring themselves down to the ground. Midrash Tanchuma adds that Israel's righteous are called "earth".

sources.quote: וּמִי הֵם הַמִּתְקַיְּמִים? הָעֲנָוִים הַנְּמוּכִים, הַמַּגִּיעִין עַצְמָם עַד לָאָרֶץ, כְּעִנְיָן שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר "וַעֲנָוִים יִרְשׁוּ אָרֶץ". וּמִדְרַשׁ תַּנְחוּמָא אוֹמֵר: כָּל־צַדִּיקֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל נִקְרְאוּ אֶרֶץ, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר, "כִּי תִהְיוּ אַתֶּם אֶרֶץ חֵפֶץ"
sources.says: Rashi asks who are the ones who last and answers the humble who lower themselves to the ground, as in "the meek shall inherit the earth", and adds that Midrash Tanchuma says all the righteous of Israel are called "earth".

1:4.headline: Maimonides: לעולם alone does not prove the earth lasts forever
1:4.body: Maimonides says the word עולם shows eternity only when paired with עד, as in "olam va'ed". So Solomon's "the earth stands forever" is weaker than David's "forever and ever". Metzudat David instead reads the line as a question: does the earth itself last forever? It too wears out like a garment.

sources.quote: מה שאתה יודע הוא, ש"עולם" אינו מצביע על נצחיות אלא כאשר מצטרף אליו "עד": אם לאחריו, כדבריו "עולם ועד", או לפניו, כדבריו "עד עולם". אם כן דברי שלמה "לְעוֹלָם עֹמָדֶת" הם למטה מדברי דוד "בַּל תִּמּוֹט עוֹלָם וָעֶד"
sources.says: Maimonides says "olam" points to eternity only when "ad" joins it, after or before, so Solomon's "le'olam omedet" is lower than David's "olam va'ed".

sources.quote: וכי הארץ עצמה לעולם עומדת הלא גם היא כבגד תבלה
sources.says: Metzudat David reads it as a question: does the earth itself stand forever, when it too wears out like a garment?

1:5.headline: The sun "pants" for its place, like a servant longing for shade
1:5.body: שואף usually means to gasp or breathe in. Metzudat Zion and Ralbag read it as longing, like a servant longing for shade. Ibn Ezra says the sun is like someone gasping for wind from desire to get home.

sources.quote: שואף. ענין ההבטה והתאוה אל הדבר כמו כעבד ישאף צל (איוב ז ב)
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says שואף means looking toward and desiring something, like "as a servant longs for shade" in Job.

sources.quote: שואף. מענין התוחלת והתקוה כטעם כעבד ישאף צל
sources.says: Ralbag says שואף comes from hope and expectation, as in "as a servant longs for shade".

sources.quote: וענין שואף. כמו באות נפשה שאפה רוח כאילו הוא שואף הרוח מרוב תאותו לשוב אל מקומו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says שואף is like "in the desire of her soul she pants for wind", as if the sun were gasping for air out of its longing to return to its place.

1:6.headline: "The ruach" goes around: wind, will, or direction?
1:6.body: Ibn Ezra says the verse is about the wind, and rejects reading הרוח as a direction. Rashi and Metzudat Zion read it as the sun's own will or spirit.

sources.quote: הָרוּחַ. רוּחוֹ שֶׁל שֶׁמֶשׁ, טלנ"ט בְּלַעַ"ז, כְּמוֹ "עַל אֲשֶׁר יִהְיֶה־שָּׁמָּה הָרוּחַ לָלֶכֶת"
sources.says: Rashi says הרוח is the sun's spirit, glossed with a French word, like "wherever the spirit was to go".

sources.quote: הרוח. ענינו רצון כמו הנני נותן בו רוח (ישעיה לז ז)
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says הרוח means will, like "I will put a spirit in him" in Isaiah.

sources.quote: ויפרש הרוח פאה וזה איננו נכון ויורה עליו ועל סביבותיו שב הרוח וכל הפסוק הוא בענין הרוח שפעם יתנועע האויר לפאת צפון ופעם לפאת דרום
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says some explain הרוח as a direction, which he says is not right, since the whole verse is about the wind, which at times moves the air north and at times south.

1:8.headline: "Devarim" here may be "things", not "words"
1:8.body: Metzudat Zion says הדברים means matters or things, like "because of the money" in Genesis. Rashi reads it as speaking: weariness comes from trading Torah study for idle talk.

sources.quote: הדברים. הענינים כמו על דבר הכסף (בראשית מג יח)
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says הדברים means matters, like "al devar hakesef" in Genesis 43.

sources.quote: אִם מַחֲלִיף הוּא עֵסֶק הַתּוֹרָה לְדַבֵּר בִּדְבָרִים בְּטֵלִים, הֲרֵי הֵם יְגֵעִים
sources.says: Rashi says that if someone swaps Torah study for speaking idle words, those words are wearying.

1:10.headline: "Olamim" here means "ages", not "eternities"
1:10.body: Ibn Ezra, Ralbag and Metzudat Zion all say עולמים means long stretches of time. Ralbag compares "he shall serve him forever", which means until the Jubilee.

sources.quote: ופירוש עולמים כמו זמנים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the meaning of עולמים is "times".

sources.quote: לעולמים. לזמנים וכמוהו ועבדו לעולם שהוא זמן היובל
sources.says: Ralbag says לעולמים means "for times", like "and he shall serve him forever", which is the time of the Jubilee.

sources.quote: ומלת עולמים יורה על זמנים רבים. כמו ועבדו לעולם (שמות כא ו)
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says עולמים points to many times, like "and he shall serve him forever" in Exodus.

1:12.headline: "I was king": a king no longer, or just a past form?
1:12.body: Rashi reads הייתי as "I was" and says Solomon is no longer king: he lost his rule step by step until only his staff was left. Metzudat Zion says a past form can describe something ongoing, like "so Job would do" in Job 1.

sources.quote: אֲנִי קֹהֶלֶת הָיִיתִי מֶלֶךְ. עַל־כָּל־הָעוֹלָם, וְלִבְסוֹף עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל, וְלִבְסוֹף עַל יְרוּשָׁלַיִם לְבַדָּהּ, וְלִבְסוֹף עַל מַקְלִי, שֶׁהֲרֵי נֶאֱמַר: "הָיִיתִי מֶלֶךְ בִּירוּשָׁלָיִם". אֲבָל עַכְשָׁיו אֵינִי מֶלֶךְ
sources.says: Rashi says Solomon was king over the whole world, then over Israel, then over Jerusalem alone, then over his staff, and that now he is no longer king.

sources.quote: הייתי. דבר ההוה נופל בו לשון עבר ולשון עתיד כמו שנאמר והלכו בניו וגו׳ ככה יעשה איוב (איוב א ה)
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says a thing that is present can take past or future language, as in "and his sons would go... so Job would do".

1:13.headline: Is "wisdom" here Torah, natural science, or understanding?
1:13.body: Rashi says he searched in the Torah, which is wisdom. Ralbag says the wisdom is natural science, knowing the causes of things. Metzudat David says he searched with wisdom and understanding, not by sight alone.

sources.quote: וְנָתַתִּי אֶת־לִבִּי לִדְרוֹשׁ. בַּתּוֹרָה, הִיא הַחָכְמָה
sources.says: Rashi says "I set my heart to seek" means in the Torah, which is the wisdom.

sources.quote: לדעת סבותיו וכל משיגיו והיא החכמה הטבעית
sources.says: Ralbag says he sought to know the causes of things and all they reach, and that this is the natural wisdom.

sources.quote: לא במראית העין, רק בחכמה ובהבנת השכל חקרתי על כל הדברים הנעשים תחת השמים
sources.says: Metzudat David says he investigated not by what the eye sees, but with wisdom and understanding of the mind, all that is done under the heavens.

1:13.headline: "An evil matter": a bad custom, a dwelling, or a thought?
1:13.body: Rashi first says עניין רע is a bad custom of theirs. He adds that עניין can come from the word for a dwelling or from the word for thought. Metzudat David says the evil is that God left people free to choose.

sources.quote: עִנְיָן רָע. מִנְהָג רַע לָהֶם
sources.says: Rashi says "inyan ra" means a bad custom for them.

sources.quote: "עִנְיָן" יֵשׁ לְפָתְרוֹ לְשׁוֹן מָעוֹן וְדִירָה, וְיֵשׁ לְפָתְרוֹ לְשׁוֹן עִיּוּן וּמַחֲשָׁבָה
sources.says: Rashi says ענין can be explained as the language of a dwelling, or as the language of study and thought.

sources.quote: רוצה לומר הבנתי שזה הוא דבר רע במה שעזב אלהים והניח כל המעשים לבני האדם בתת להם הבחירה
sources.says: Metzudat David says he understood it to be a bad thing that God left all deeds to people by giving them free choice.

1:15.headline: "Lacking" means missing from the count of the upright
1:15.body: Rashi says the one who made himself lacking leaves the group of the upright, and cannot be counted with them when they receive their reward. Metzudat David says it is a lack in his deeds that he cannot make whole.

sources.quote: זֶה שֶׁחִסֵּר עַצְמוֹ מִמִּנְיַן הַכְּשֵׁרִים, לֹא יוּכַל לְהִמָּנוֹת עִמָּהֶם בְּקִבּוּל שְׂכָרָם
sources.says: Rashi says this is one who made himself lacking from the number of the upright, and cannot be counted with them in receiving their reward.

sources.quote: דבר הנחסר במעשיו, אין בידו להשלימו להיות נמנה במנין הדברים אשר לא חסרו
sources.says: Metzudat David says it is something lacking in his deeds, which he cannot complete so as to be counted among the things that were not lacking.

1:17.headline: הוללות means a mixed-up, confused mind
1:17.body: Rashi says it is dullness and confusion of mind, from the word for mixing, as in "mixed with water". Metzudat Zion says the same, and points to "he makes judges foolish" in Job.

sources.quote: הֹלֵלוֹת. שִׁעֲמוּם וְטֵרוּף הַדַּעַת, לְשׁוֹן עִרְבּוּב, כְּמוֹ "מָהוּל בַּמָּיִם"
sources.says: Rashi says הוללות is dullness and madness of the mind, from the language of mixing, like "mixed with water".

sources.quote: הוללות. ענין שיעמום וערבוב הדעת כמו ושופטים יהולל (איוב יב וז)
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says הוללות means dullness and confusion of the mind, like "and judges he makes fools" in Job.

1:17.headline: ושכלות is a spelling of סכלות, "foolishness"
1:17.body: The word looks like "intellect", but it means the opposite. Metzudat Zion and Ralbag say it is the same as סכלות with a samech, and Rashi glosses it as foolishness.

sources.quote: ושכלות. כמו וסכלות בסמ״ך, והוא ענין שטות
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says ושכלות is like וסכלות with a samech, and means foolishness.

sources.quote: הוללות ושכלות. הוא כמו סכלות בסמ״ך
sources.says: Ralbag says הוללות ושכלות is like סכלות with a samech.

sources.quote: וְשִׂכְלוּת. שְׁטוּת
sources.says: Rashi glosses ושכלות as foolishness.

10:1.headline: Spoiled perfume: does it bubble up, or keep pouring out a stink?
10:1.body: Ibn Ezra calls יביע a hard word here. Rashi says it means the oil foams up in bubbles. Ibn Ezra reads it from מבוע, a spring: the stink keeps flowing out.

sources.quote: וְנִרְאֶה בוֹ כְמִין אֲבַעְבּוּעוֹת, וְזֶהוּ מַשְׁמָעוֹ שֶׁל יַבִּיעַ
sources.says: Rashi says the oil looks as if it has bubbles, and that is the meaning of יביע.

sources.quote: ומלת יביע קשה במקום במקום הזה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the word is difficult in this place.

sources.quote: והקרוב אלי היותו ממבוע
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the reading closest to him is that it comes from מבוע, a spring.

10:1.headline: Precious, or heavy? A little folly outweighs wisdom
10:1.body: יקר usually means precious. Rashi reads it as 'heavy': a little foolishness weighs more than wisdom and honor and tips the scale. Metzudat Zion keeps the usual sense, worth or importance.

sources.quote: לְשׁוֹן כּוֹבֶד. הוּא כָבֵד וְשָׁקוּל יוֹתֵר מִן הַחָכְמָה שֶׁבּוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says the word means heaviness: the folly is heavier than the wisdom in the person.

sources.quote: יקר. ענין חשיבות כמו אבנים יקרות
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means importance, as in 'precious stones'.

10:1.headline: The 'flies of death' stand for the urge to do wrong
10:1.body: On the surface this is about dead flies spoiling perfume. Rashi brings a midrash, and the Targum agrees, that the flies stand for the evil urge.

sources.quote: וּמִדְרַשׁ אַגָּדָה מוֹשְׁלִים יֵצֶר הָרַע לִזְבוּבֵי מָוֶת
sources.says: Rashi says a midrash compares the evil inclination to deadly flies.

sources.quote: וְיִצְרָא בִּישָׁא דְּשָׁכֵין עַל תַּרְעֵי לִבָּא הֵי כִדְבוּבָא
sources.says: The Targum says the evil inclination, which sits at the gates of the heart, is like a fly.

10:4.headline: Healing, or holding back? Two readings of מרפא
10:4.body: Rashi reads מרפא as healing: the suffering that comes on you cures your sins. Metzudat Zion reads it from רפיון, slackness or letting go.

sources.quote: מַרְפֵּא הוּא לַעֲוֹנוֹתֶיךָ
sources.says: Rashi says the hardships that come on you are a cure for your sins.

sources.quote: מרפא. מלשון רפיון
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the word comes from slackness.

10:6.headline: Folly set up high, or should the word read 'wisdom'?
10:6.body: הסכל, folly, appears only here. Ibn Ezra reports that some wanted to read it with a ש, as שכל, wisdom. He rejects this: the verse means a fool was set in high places.

sources.quote: מפרשים אמרו שהיה ראוי להיות בשי״ן
sources.says: Ibn Ezra reports that some commentators said the word should be spelled with a shin.

sources.quote: וכן פירושו נתן איש הסכל שהוא הכסיל להיות במרומים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the plain sense is that the foolish man was placed on high.

sources.quote: והרצון נתן איש הסכל והוא הסכלות
sources.says: Ralbag says the word 'man' is left out: the man of folly was set on high.

10:6.headline: The 'rich' brought low: rich in wisdom, or Israel?
10:6.body: Ralbag says the rich here are rich in wisdom, because the verse sets them against folly. Rashi reads them as Israel, who will one day sit low.

sources.quote: הם עשירים בחכמה כי הוא מקביל לסכלות
sources.says: Ralbag says they are rich in wisdom, since the word stands opposite folly.

sources.quote: יִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁכָּל הַגְּדֻלָּה וְהַכָּבוֹד
sources.says: Rashi says the rich are Israel, whose greatness and honor will be brought low.

10:11.headline: 'Master of the tongue': snake charmer or slanderer?
10:11.body: Rashi reads בעל הלשון as the snake charmer, who gains nothing if he keeps quiet and the snake bites. Metzudat Zion reads it as a slanderer, and Metzudat David says he is even worse than the snake.

sources.quote: לֶחָבֵר הָרָשָׁע שֶׁהָיָה רָגִיל לְלָחְשׁוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says there is no gain for the wicked charmer who used to whisper over the snake.

sources.quote: לבעל הלשון. זה המלשין ומדבר לשון הרע
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it is the informer who speaks evil of others.

sources.quote: וכאומר שהוא עוד גרוע מן הנחש
sources.says: Metzudat David says the slanderer is even worse than the snake.

10:17.headline: 'Son of nobles', or 'son of the white ones'?
10:17.body: Metzudat Zion says חורים are nobles, as in Nehemiah. Ibn Ezra reports one reading that links it to חור, white: great people are compared to light and the lowly to darkness.

sources.quote: בן חורים. כן יקראו הגדולים אנשי השם
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the great and famous are called חורים.

sources.quote: ויפרש חורים לבנים כמו חור כרפס ותכלת
sources.says: Ibn Ezra reports a commentator who explains חורים as white, as in 'white, green and blue' in Esther.

10:17.headline: A one-time word: drinking, or weakness?
10:17.body: בשתי appears only here. Rashi and Ralbag read it as drinking wine, from שתה. Ibn Ezra also brings a reading of weakness, from a word for drying up.

sources.quote: וְלֹא בִשְׁתִיַּת יָיִן
sources.says: Rashi says the princes deal in the strength of wisdom, not in drinking wine.

sources.quote: בשתי. הוא מן שתה ועניינו שתיה
sources.says: Ralbag says the word comes from שתה and means drinking.

sources.quote: כי בשתי כענין דלות כמו ונשתו לשונם
sources.says: Ibn Ezra reports that some read it as weakness, as in 'their tongue dried up'.

10:18.headline: Laziness in the 'pair' form: two lazy hands
10:18.body: בעצלתים has the ending Hebrew uses for pairs, like eyes or hands. Metzudat Zion and Ibn Ezra say it means a pair of lazy hands.

sources.quote: ורוצה לומר ידים עצלתים, ולזה אמר בלשון רבים
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means lazy hands, which is why it is in the plural form.

sources.quote: תהיה מלת עצלתים חוזרת לידים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the word refers back to the hands.

10:20.headline: Not even in your thoughts, or not even to a relative?
10:20.body: Rashi and Metzudat Zion read במדעך as 'in your thoughts': do not curse the king even in your mind. Ralbag adds a second reading, from מודע, a kinsman, as in Ruth: do not curse him even to a relative you trust.

sources.quote: אֲפִילּוּ בְמַחְשְׁבוֹתֶיךָ, בְּלֹא דִבּוּר
sources.says: Rashi says it means even in your thoughts, without speaking.

sources.quote: או יהיה מדעך כמו מודעך מענין ולנעמי מודע לאישה
sources.says: Ralbag says it may mean your kinsman, as in 'Naomi had a kinsman of her husband'.

10:20.headline: The bird that carries your words: overstatement, or your soul?
10:20.body: Maimonides says the bird carrying your voice is an exaggeration, a way of speaking the prophets use often. Rashi reads the bird as your own soul, which will one day fly up to heaven.

sources.quote: ומסוג ההגזמה הוא מה שנאמר
sources.says: Maimonides lists this verse as an example of exaggeration in scripture.

sources.quote: נְשָׁמָה הַנְּתוּנָה בְךָ, שֶׁסּוֹפָה לָעוּף עַל הַשָּׁמָיִם
sources.says: Rashi says the bird is the soul within you, which will in the end fly to heaven.

sources.quote: כי עוף השמים. דרך משל
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the bird is a figure of speech.

12:2.headline: The darkening sun: an aging body, or a fallen kingdom
12:2.body: Verses 2 to 6 describe a world going dark. Rashi, following the sages, reads it as a picture of the aging body: the sun is the forehead that once glowed. A second midrash he brings reads it as the nation: the sun is the kingdom of David.

sources.quote: זוּ פַדַּחַת, שֶׁהִיא מְאִירָה וּמַצְהֶבֶת בְּאָדָם בָּחוּר
sources.says: Rashi says the sun is the forehead, which shines in a young man and dulls in old age.

sources.quote: זוּ מַלְכוּת בֵּית דָּוִד
sources.says: Rashi brings a midrash that the sun is the kingdom of the house of David.

12:3.headline: The 'grinders' that stop: teeth, or the great teachings
12:3.body: הטחנות are women who grind grain. Rashi and Metzudat David say they are the teeth, which grow few in old age. A midrash Rashi brings reads them as the great collections of Mishnah, which fell out of study.

sources.quote: וּבָטְלוּ הַטֹּחֲנוֹת. אֵלּוּ הַשִּׁנַּיִם
sources.says: Rashi says the grinders are the teeth.

sources.quote: הם השינים הטוחנות את המאכל
sources.says: Metzudat David says they are the teeth that grind food.

sources.quote: אֵלּוּ הַמִּשְׁנַיּוֹת הַגְּדוֹלוֹת
sources.says: Rashi brings a midrash that they are the great Mishnah collections of Rabbi Akiva, Rabbi Chiya and Bar Kappara.

12:5.headline: A doubled word for doubled fear
12:5.body: חתחתים appears only here. It repeats the letters of חת, terror. Metzudat Zion says the doubling means great fear, the way אדמדם means very red.

sources.quote: ונכפלו הפ״א והעי״ן הפעל ויורה על פחד הרבה כמו אדמדם
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the root letters are doubled to show great fear, like אדמדם for very red.

sources.quote: לָשׁוֹן כָּפוּל הוּא בַתֵּבָה, כְּמוֹ גַּלְגַּלִּים
sources.says: Rashi says it is a doubled word, like גלגלים.

sources.quote: אֵימוֹת וְחִתּוֹת הַרְבֵּה בַדְּרָכִים
sources.says: Rashi says it means many terrors on the road.

12:5.headline: The locust grows heavy: a bug, or a part of the body?
12:5.body: Metzudat David reads it plainly: even a locust landing on him feels like a heavy load. Rashi reads חגב as the buttocks, which feel like a burden. Ibn Ezra says it is the ankle.

sources.quote: אם ישכון עליו חגב תכבד עליו כסובל משא כבד
sources.says: Metzudat David says if a locust settles on him it feels like a heavy load.

sources.quote: אֵלּוּ הָעֲגָבוֹת
sources.says: Rashi says it means the buttocks.

sources.quote: ויסתבל החגב. הקרסול
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means the ankle.

12:6.headline: Written 'moves away', read 'chained': the silver cord
12:6.body: The word is written ירחק, 'moves away', but read ירתק. Rashi ties it to the 'silver chains' in Isaiah: at death the cord twists up like a chain. Ralbag reads it as 'snapped'.

sources.quote: יֵרָתֵק לְשׁוֹן רְתֻקוֹת כֶּסֶף
sources.says: Rashi says the word is like 'chains of silver'.

sources.quote: וּמִתְעַקֵּם בְּתוֹךְ הַחֻלְיוֹת וְנַעֲשֶׂה כְשַׁלְשֶׁלֶת
sources.says: Rashi says the cord bends inside the vertebrae and becomes like a chain.

sources.quote: ירתק. ישבר ויחתך
sources.says: Ralbag says it means broken and cut.

12:7.headline: The spirit that returns to God is what survives death
12:7.body: רוח can mean wind, breath, or spirit. Maimonides lists this verse for the sense of what remains of a person after death and does not perish. Ibn Ezra says the verse refutes those who think the spirit is only a passing quality of the body.

sources.quote: הוא גם שם הדבר הנשאר מן האדם אחרי המוות
sources.says: Maimonides says רוח is also the name for what remains of a person after death, and cites this verse.

sources.quote: זה הפסוק יכחיש האומרים שהרוח היא מקרה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says this verse refutes those who say the spirit is a mere accident, since an accident cannot return.

12:8.headline: 'The Kohelet': a title for the one who gathers
12:8.body: קהלת comes from קהל, to gather. Rashi says it means the one in whom wisdom was gathered. Ibn Ezra notes that here it takes 'the', which shows it is a title, not a personal name.

sources.quote: מִי שֶׁבּוֹ קְבוּצַת הַחָכְמָה
sources.says: Rashi says Kohelet is the one in whom wisdom is gathered.

sources.quote: הקהלת. ענין אסיפה וקבוץ
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the word means gathering.

sources.quote: ובא ה״א הידיעה על קהלת בעבור היותו תואר השם
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it takes the definite article because it is a description, not a proper name.

12:14.headline: Judged for 'everything hidden': mistakes, or the heart's intent?
12:14.body: Rashi says the hidden things are sins done by mistake, without knowing. Ibn Ezra and Metzudat David say every visible act is judged by the hidden intent of the heart.

sources.quote: אֲפִילוּ עַל הַשּׁוֹגֵג
sources.says: Rashi says it means even unintentional sins.

sources.quote: יובא במשפט כפי הנעלם והענין כפי כונת הלב
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says each act is judged by what is hidden, meaning the heart's intent.

sources.quote: לא לפי הנראה לבני האדם, רק כפי כוונת הלב
sources.says: Metzudat David says the judgment is not by what people see but by the intent of the heart.

2:5.headline: פרדסים: orchards of fruit trees, or groves of one kind?
2:5.body: Metzudat Zion says גנות are places for vegetables and flowers, and פרדסים are places planted with fruit trees. Ibn Ezra says a גן has many kinds of trees, while a פרדס has one kind, like פרדס רמונים.

sources.quote: גנות. מקום זרוע ירקות ופרחים
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says גנות are places sown with vegetables and flowers.

sources.quote: ופרדסים. מקום נטוע אילנות בעלי פרי
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says פרדסים are places planted with fruit-bearing trees.

sources.quote: והגן יש בו אילנים רבים ממינים רבים והפרדס הוא ממין אחד והראיה פרדס רמונים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says a garden has many trees of many kinds, and a פרדס is of one kind, as the proof פרדס רמונים shows.

2:6.headline: יער צומח עצים: a forest of fruitless trees, or the common people?
2:6.body: Ibn Ezra and Metzudat David say it is a forest of trees that bear no fruit, such as cedars and cypresses. Rashi, in his comment on this phrase, says it means the common people, for working fields and vineyards.

sources.quote: להשקות יער צומח עצים שאין להם פירות כמו ארזים וברושים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it is to water a forest of growing trees that have no fruit, like cedars and cypresses.

sources.quote: היער המצמיח אילני סרק
sources.says: Metzudat David says it is the forest that grows barren trees.

sources.quote: יַעַר צוֹמֵחַ עֵצִים. עַמֵּי הָאָרֶץ לִמְלֶאכֶת שָׂדוֹת וּכְרָמִים
sources.says: Rashi says יער צומח עצים means the common people, for the work of fields and vineyards.

2:7.headline: בני בית: house-born servants, or stewards?
2:7.body: Ibn Ezra says בני בית are servants born in his house. Metzudat David says they are the ones in charge of the household's needs, who do not work like a slave or maidservant.

sources.quote: קניתי. ובני בית שנולדו בביתי
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says בני בית are those born in my house.

sources.quote: הם הממונים על צרכי הבית להשגיח בדבר הצורך ולא יעשו מלאכה כעבד ושפחה
sources.says: Metzudat David says they are those in charge of the house's needs, who do not do labor like a slave or maidservant.

2:10.headline: וזה היה חלקי: the joy, or his staff or cup?
2:10.body: Metzudat David says the joy alone was his share from all his toil. Rashi says that after all this, only this was left to him, and cites Rav and Shmuel: one says his staff, the other his cup.

sources.quote: השמחה לבדה היה חלקי מכל עמלי
sources.says: Metzudat David says the joy alone was my share from all my toil.

sources.quote: וְאַחֲרֵי עֲשׂוֹתִי כָל־אֵלֶּה, אֵין לִי מִכֻּלָּם אֶלָּא זֶה. רַב וּשְׁמוּאֵל, חַד אָמַר מַקְלוֹ, וְחַד אָמַר קִידוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says that after doing all this I have only this from them all, and Rav and Shmuel say it is his staff or his cup.

2:11.headline: רעות רוח: a broken will
2:11.body: Metzudat Zion says רעות means breaking and רוח means will, so רעות רוח is a broken will. Metzudat David says he wanted all this to last, and his will was broken because it did not.

sources.quote: ורעות. ענין שבירה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says ורעות means breaking.

sources.quote: ורעות רוח. שבר רצון
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says ורעות רוח is a breaking of the will.

sources.quote: כי בעשותי כל אלה היה הרצון שיהיו מתמידים, ונשבר הרצון כי לא כן הוא
sources.says: Metzudat David says that in doing all this my will was that they would last, and the will was broken since it is not so.

2:12.headline: עשוהו: "others made it", or God and his court made him?
2:12.body: Ibn Ezra reads עשוהו as "others have already made it", leaving out who did it. In the Guide, Maimonides cites a midrash: it does not say עשהו but עשוהו, as if God and his court decided on each limb of you and set you on your base.

sources.quote: וכל מה שיעשה כבר עשוהו אחרים ויחסר מלת העושים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says everything he does others have already done, and the word for the doers is left out.

sources.quote: אֵת אֲשֶׁר כְּבָר עָשָׂהוּ' – לא נאמר כָּן, אלא 'עָשׂוּהוּ' (קהלת ב,יב), כביכול הוא ובית דינו נמנו על כל אבר ואבר שבך והושיבו אותו על כנו
sources.says: Maimonides quotes the midrash: it does not say עשהו but עשוהו, as if he and his court counted every limb of you and set it in its place.

2:14.headline: עיניו בראשו: looks ahead to the end, or sees from high up?
2:14.body: Rashi says the wise man at the start of a matter looks to see how it will end. Metzudat David says his eyes are set high in his head so he can see far. Ibn Ezra says he is like a clear-sighted man.

sources.quote: בִּתְחִלַּת הַדָּבָר, מִסְתַּכֵּל מַה־יְהֵא בְסוֹפָהּ
sources.says: Rashi says at the start of a matter he looks to see what will be at its end.

sources.quote: הלא החכם יודע ומכיר שעיניו קבועות בראשו במקום גבוה למען יסתכלו למרחוק
sources.says: Metzudat David says the wise man knows his eyes are set in his head, in a high place, so they look far.

sources.quote: דמה החכם לפקח שיש לו עינים בראשו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says he likens the wise man to a clear-sighted person who has eyes in his head.

2:15.headline: Rashi reads "the fool" as "the wicked"
2:15.body: Rashi paraphrases כמקרה הכסיל as "like the fate of the wicked", and asks why be righteous. On verse 13 he also says the "folly" is the wickedness. Metzudat David keeps it to wisdom: what good is it to me that I was wise.

sources.quote: כְּמִקְרֵה הָרָשָׁע גַּם אֲנִי יִקְרֵנֵי, וְלָמָּה אֶהְיֶה צַדִּיק אָז יוֹתֵר
sources.says: Rashi says: like the fate of the wicked will happen to me too, so why should I be more righteous then?

sources.quote: מִן־הַסִּכְלוּת. הוּא הָרֶשַׁע
sources.says: Rashi says מן הסכלות is the wickedness.

sources.quote: מה תועלת בא לי עתה אחר המיתה במה שחכמתי אז
sources.says: Metzudat David says what benefit comes to me now after death from my having been wise then.

2:16.headline: בשכבר: the ש stands for אשר, or the word means הן?
2:16.body: Metzudat David says the ש in בשכבר stands for אשר. Maimonides also says ש can mean אשר, and cites שכבר in Ecclesiastes. Ibn Ezra says this word is found only in this book, and that it is better read as meaning הן.

sources.quote: והשי״ן של בשכבר הוא במקום אשר
sources.says: Metzudat David says the ש of בשכבר is in place of אשר.

sources.quote: והשי"ן היא במשמעות "אשר", כמו "שֶׁכְּבָר" (קהלת ד,ב)
sources.says: Maimonides says the ש has the meaning of אשר, like שכבר in Ecclesiastes 4:2.

sources.quote: ומלת בשכבר בענינה אינה נמצאת בכל המקרא רק בספר הזה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the word בשכבר, in this sense, is not found in all of Scripture except this book.

sources.quote: ויותר נכון היות פירושו כמו הן
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it is more right that its meaning is like הן.

2:16.headline: ואיך ימות החכם: a bitter fact, or a question that denies it?
2:16.body: Ibn Ezra reads it as a bitter fact: the wise man dies with the fool. Metzudat David reads it as a question: how can the wise man's death be like the fool's, when one is remembered with praise and the other with shame? Rashi says he sees the righteous succeed in their deaths and help their children.

sources.quote: והרעה הקשה שימות החכם עם הכסיל
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the harsh evil is that the wise man dies with the fool.

sources.quote: ואיך אפשר להדמות מיתת החכם עם מיתת הכסיל הואיל וזכרון מיתתו של זה היא סיבה אל השבח ושל זה אל הגנאי
sources.says: Metzudat David says how can the death of the wise man be like the death of the fool, when the memory of one's death leads to praise and of the other to shame.

sources.quote: אֲנִי רוֹאֶה הַצַּדִּיקִים מַצְלִיחִים בְּמִיתָתָם וּמוֹעִילִים לִבְנֵיהֶם
sources.says: Rashi says I see the righteous succeed in their deaths and benefit their children.

2:17.headline: החיים: life itself, or the living of a wicked generation?
2:17.body: Metzudat David says he hates life itself while he still lives. Rashi says he is prophesying about the generation of Rehoboam, who were wicked. Ibn Ezra says החיים here is an adjective, "the living".

sources.quote: אני שונא וממאס את החיים אשר עודני חי
sources.says: Metzudat David says I hate and reject life, while I am still alive.

sources.quote: שֶׁהָיָה מִתְנַבֵּא עַל דּוֹרוֹ שֶׁל רְחַבְעָם שֶׁהָיוּ רְשָׁעִים
sources.says: Rashi says he was prophesying about the generation of Rehoboam, who were wicked.

sources.quote: והחיים בפסוק הזה הוא שם התואר
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says החיים in this verse is an adjective.

2:24.headline: אין טוב באדם: a question, or "nothing good except eating"?
2:24.body: Rashi and Metzudat David read it as a question: is there not good in a man who eats and drinks? Ibn Ezra reads it as a statement and adds the missing רק: there is nothing good for a man except to eat and drink.

sources.quote: אֵין טוֹב בָּאָדָם. בִּתְמִיהַּ, שֶׁיֹּאכַל וְיִשְׁתֶּה וְיַרְאֶה אֶת־נַפְשׁוֹ טוֹב
sources.says: Rashi says אין טוב באדם is a question of astonishment: that he eat and drink and show his soul good.

sources.quote: אין טוב באדם. בתמיה וכי אין זה דבר טוב באדם שיאכל וישתה כאות נפשו
sources.says: Metzudat David says it is a question: is it not a good thing in a man that he eat and drink as his soul desires?

sources.quote: ויחסר מקום רק או הדומה לו וכן הוא אין טוב באדם רק שיאכל וישתה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the word רק or something like it is missing, so it is: there is no good in a man except that he eat and drink.

2:24.headline: והראה את נפשו טוב: enjoy, or do justice and charity?
2:24.body: Rashi says he gives his heart to doing justice and charity along with his food and drink. Metzudat David says to do charity and kindness with the wealth. Ibn Ezra says the only good this toil gives is food and drink.

sources.quote: כְּלוֹמַר, יִתֵּן לִבּוֹ לַעֲשׂוֹת מִשְׁפָּט וּצְדָקָה עִם הַמַּאֲכָל וְהַמִּשְׁתֶּה
sources.says: Rashi says that is, he will set his heart to do justice and charity along with food and drink.

sources.quote: ולהראות טוב לנפשו בהעושר הבא לו בעמל, רוצה לומר לעשות בו צדקה וחסד
sources.says: Metzudat David says to show good to his soul with the wealth that came through toil, meaning to do charity and kindness with it.

sources.quote: טוב לא מצא זה העמל בכל יגיעתו חוץ מן המאכל והמשתה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says this toiler found no good in all his labor except food and drink.

2:25.headline: יחוש: hurry, or feel?
2:25.body: Rashi and Ibn Ezra read it as hurrying: who is quicker to swallow it than I? Metzudat Zion says it is from חשש, and Ralbag says it means "who will feel".

sources.quote: וּמִי יְמַהֵר לְבָלְעָהּ מִבַּלְעָדָי
sources.says: Rashi says and who will hurry to swallow it besides me?

sources.quote: ויחוש הוא למהר לכל תאותו כמו מהרה חושה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says יחוש means to hurry to all his desire, like מהרה חושה.

sources.quote: יחוש. הוא מלשון חשש הידוע בדברי רז״ל
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says יחוש is from חשש, known in the sages' words.

sources.quote: ומי יחוש. ר"ל ומי ירגיש
sources.says: Ralbag says ומי יחוש means and who will feel.

2:25.headline: חוץ here is the sages' word for "apart from"
2:25.body: Ibn Ezra says this use of חוץ, meaning "apart from", is not found elsewhere in Scripture, only in the words of the early sages. Rashi glosses it as מבלעדי.

sources.quote: וכן ענין חוץ ואין כלשון הזה במקרא כי אם בדברי הקדמונים מעתיקי המצות
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says so too the sense of חוץ: this language is not in Scripture, only in the words of the early sages.

sources.quote: חוּץ מִמֶּנִּי. מִבַּלְעָדָי
sources.says: Rashi says חוץ ממני means besides me.

3:1.headline: חפץ: every thing, or every thing a person wants
3:1.body: Rashi says חפץ here simply means 'thing', as in the Hebrew of the Mishnah. Metzudat David reads it as desire: people want one thing at one time and its opposite at another, and the list that follows shows this.

sources.quote: לְכָל־דָּבָר. כָּל־הַדְּבָרִים קְרוּיִם חֲפָצִים בִּלְשׁוֹן מִשְׁנָה
sources.says: Rashi says it means every thing, since in the Mishnah's language all things are called חפצים.

sources.quote: לכל הדברים שהאדם חפץ בו גם לזה יש עת, כי לא בכל עת יחפוץ בדבר אחד כי פעם יחפוץ בדבר מה ופעם בחלופו
sources.says: Metzudat David says everything a person desires has its time, because a person wants one thing at one time and its opposite at another.

3:5.headline: A time to embrace: human desire, or God holding Israel close
3:5.body: Ibn Ezra says even the desire planted in people has its time, to embrace and to keep away. Rashi reads it as God holding Israel close like a belt, and later sending them far away.

sources.quote: אפילו התאוה הנטועה ברוח בן אדם יש לה עת
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says even the desire planted in a person's spirit has its proper time.

sources.quote: כִּי כַּאֲשֶׁר יִדְבַּק הָאֵזוֹר
sources.says: Rashi points to Jeremiah 13:11: as a belt clings to a person, so God held Israel close.

sources.quote: וְרִחַק ה' אֶת־הָאָדָם
sources.says: Rashi points to Isaiah 6:12, where God sends the people far away.

3:7.headline: Aaron's silence earned him God's word
3:7.body: Rashi says sometimes a person is rewarded for keeping quiet. Aaron was silent, and he earned that God spoke to him alone.

sources.quote: פְּעָמִים שֶׁאָדָם שׁוֹתֵק וּמְקַבֵּל שָׂכָר, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר, "וַיִּדֹּם אַהֲרֹן", וְזָכָה שֶׁנִּתְיַחֵד הַדִּבּוּר עִמּוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says a person is sometimes silent and rewarded for it: Aaron was silent, and God then spoke to him alone.

sources.quote: לבל ישיב דבר למחרפו
sources.says: Metzudat David says the time to be silent is not answering someone who insults you.

3:11.headline: The world in their heart, or hiddenness in their heart
3:11.body: העלם is spelled here without a vav, and Rashi reads it as hiddenness: God hid the day of death, so people still build and plant. Ibn Ezra reads עולם as lasting time: people act as if they will live forever.

sources.quote: וּלְכַךְ, כָּתוּב כַּאן "הָעֹלָם" חָסֵר, לְשׁוֹן הָעֲלָמָה, שֶׁאִם יֵדַע הָאָדָם יוֹם מִיתָתוֹ קְרוֹבָה, לֹא יִבְנֶה בַיִת וְלֹא יִטַּע כֶּרֶם
sources.says: Rashi says the word is spelled short to mean hiding: if people knew their death was near, they would not build a house or plant a vineyard.

sources.quote: וענין גם את העולם נתן בלבם שבני אדם מתעסקי' כאילו יחיו לעולם
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means people busy themselves as if they will live forever.

3:18.headline: God tests people, or God chose people
3:18.body: Rashi and Metzudat Zion read לברם as sorting or testing: God shows proud rulers their power is nothing. Ibn Ezra reads it from 'choose': God chose humans out of all creatures, yet in their thoughts they act like animals.

sources.quote: לברם. מלשון ברור דבר ובחינה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the word means sorting and testing.

sources.quote: לְהוֹדִיעָם שֶׁאֵין שְׂרָרוֹתָם כְּלוּם
sources.says: Rashi says God makes known to them that their rule is nothing.

sources.quote: בעבור בני האדם שבחרם האלהים מכל תולדות הארץ וראיתי שהם כמו בהמות הם לנפשם במחשבותם
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says God chose humans from all the earth's creatures, yet he saw they are like animals in their thoughts.

3:19.headline: No edge over animals? Rashi and Metzudat David limit the claim
3:19.body: The verse says people have no advantage over animals. Rashi says the advantage just cannot be seen once a person dies, and Metzudat David says it is true only of one who chased wealth, not of one who studied Torah and did good.

sources.quote: וְיִתְרוֹנוֹ וְהַצְּלָחָתוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם יוֹתֵר מִן הַבְּהֵמָה אֵינוֹ נִרְאֶה מִשֶׁמֵּת
sources.says: Rashi says a person's advantage over an animal cannot be seen after death.

sources.quote: זהו אם כל מעשה אדם היה הבל שלא עסק כי אם באסיפת הקנינים וכדומה, אבל לא כן הוא אם עסק בתורה ובמעשים טובים
sources.says: Metzudat David says this holds only if a person spent his life gathering possessions, not if he studied Torah and did good deeds.

3:21.headline: Does the human spirit rise? The vowels say it does
3:21.body: This can sound like doubt: who knows whether the human spirit goes up? Ibn Ezra says the vowel under the ה marks 'the', not a question, and Rashi reads it as: few take to heart that the human spirit rises to face judgment.

sources.quote: וה"א העולה היא למעלה קמץ גם יש דגוש ביו"ד שאחרי ה"א הידיע' כמו היושב' ואילו היה לתימ' היה שוא ופתח תחת הה"א
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the ה here has the vowel of 'the', and a question would have had a different vowel.

sources.quote: מִי הוּא אֲשֶׁר מֵבִין וְנוֹתֵן לֵב שֶׁרוּחַ בְּנֵי אָדָם הִיא הָעוֹלָה לְמַעְלָה וְעוֹמֶדֶת בְּדִין
sources.says: Rashi says it asks who takes to heart that the human spirit goes up and stands in judgment.

4:3.headline: Not Eden: עדן here means 'until now'
4:3.body: The letters spell Eden, but here the word means 'yet' or 'until now'. Ibn Ezra says it is two words joined, עד and הנה, with letters dropped.

sources.quote: עדן. עדיין
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says עדן means 'still' or 'yet'.

sources.quote: מלת עדן מורכב׳ והיא חסר׳ ה״א לפני הנו״ן
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says עדן is a joined word, missing a ה before the נ, the same as עדנה in the verse before.

sources.quote: חסר ה״א והוא עד הנה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the word is missing a ה and means עד הנה, 'until now'.

4:4.headline: Toil, or sin? Rashi reads עמל as wrongdoing
4:4.body: עמל usually means hard work or trouble. Rashi says here it means sins, which are trouble in God's eyes.

sources.quote: הֵן הָעֲבֵרוֹת, שֶׁהֵן עָמָל בְּעֵינֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
sources.says: Rashi says these are sins, which are trouble in the eyes of God.

sources.quote: הם העבירות שהמה עמל בעיני המקום ורע לפניו
sources.says: Metzudat David also says these are sins, which are trouble and evil before God.

4:10.headline: Not 'but if': ואילו here means 'woe to him'
4:10.body: ואילו looks like the word for 'but if'. The commentators read it as two words, ואי לו, 'and woe to him', the one who falls with no one to lift him.

sources.quote: וְאִי לוֹ. וְאוֹי לוֹ
sources.says: Rashi reads it as ואי לו, meaning 'woe to him'.

sources.quote: ואוי לו וכן אי לך ארץ
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means 'woe to him', like 'woe to you, land' later in the book.

sources.quote: ומלת כמו אוי ואין לה דומה כי אם בספר הזה אי לך ארץ
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the word is like אוי, 'woe', and its only other use is in this book, 'woe to you, land'.

4:13.headline: The poor wise child is the good inclination
4:13.body: Rashi and the sages read the 'poor and wise child' as the good inclination. Rashi says it is called a child because it arrives only at age thirteen.

sources.quote: זֶה יֵצֶר טוֹב, וְלָמָּה נִקְרָא שְׁמוֹ יֶלֶד? שֶׁאֵינוֹ בָא בְאָדָם עַד י"ג שָׁנָה
sources.says: Rashi says this is the good inclination, called a child because it does not come into a person until age thirteen.

sources.quote: ונקרא יצר טוב "יֶלֶד מִסְכֵּן וְחָכָם"
sources.says: The Guide cites the sages: the evil inclination is called a 'great king' and the good inclination a 'poor and wise child'.

4:14.headline: 'Born poor' here means the king became poor
4:14.body: נולד usually means 'was born'. Rashi says here it means 'became', and Ralbag says it means something new that happens, so the foolish king ends up poor.

sources.quote: נוֹלַד. נַעֲשָׂה, וּלְשׁוֹן הֹוֶה הוּא
sources.says: Rashi says נולד means 'became', in the present tense.

sources.quote: הוא מענין ילד יום שהרצון בו הדבר שיתחדש ויקרה ביום ההוא
sources.says: Ralbag compares 'what a day may bring forth': the word means something new that happens, here that the king becomes poor.

5:5.headline: לחטיא: to make something miss, or go missing
5:5.body: חטא first means to miss a target, as in Judges' 'and did not miss'. The Metzudat Zion reads it here as making something lacking: a broken vow can take your children from the world.

sources.quote: לחטיא. ענין חסרון כמו ולא יחטיא
sources.says: The Metzudat Zion says the word means lacking, as in 'and did not miss' in Judges.

sources.quote: כי זה יהיה סבה להחסיר את בניך מן העולם
sources.says: The Metzudat David says the vow could cause your children to be missing from the world.

5:5.headline: Before 'the angel': a heavenly scribe, or the charity collector?
5:5.body: Rashi and the Metzudat David say the מלאך is the collector who comes for the charity you pledged in public. Ibn Ezra says it is an angel who writes down every word a person says.

sources.quote: שָׁלִיחַ הַבָּא לְתָבְעֲךָ צְדָקָה שֶׁפָּסַקְתָּ בְּרַבִּים
sources.says: Rashi says it is the messenger who comes to collect the charity you pledged in public.

sources.quote: הגזבר של ההקדש הבא לתובעך הצדקה שנדרת ופסקת ברבים
sources.says: The Metzudat David says it is the Temple treasurer who comes to collect the charity you vowed in public.

sources.quote: ומלאך ממשרתיו ממונה לכתוב בספר כל הדבורים היוצאים מפי האדם
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says an angel, one of God's servants, is appointed to write in a book every word a person speaks.

5:7.headline: God 'keeps': watching the oppressors, or waiting them out?
5:7.body: Rashi gives both senses of שמר: God sees what the oppressors do, and he waits until their measure of sin is full. The Metzudat Zion reads it as waiting, as in 'his father kept the matter'.

sources.quote: כִּי גָבֹהַּ מֵעַל גָּבֹהַּ שֹׁמֵר. וְרוֹאֶה אֶת־מַעֲשֵׂיהֶם
sources.says: Rashi says the One above watches and sees their deeds.

sources.quote: מַמְתִּין עַד שֶׁתִּתְמַלֵּא סְאָתָם
sources.says: Rashi says he waits until their measure is full.

sources.quote: שומר. ממתין כמו ואביו שמר את הדבר
sources.says: The Metzudat Zion says שמר means waits, as in 'his father kept the matter'.

5:8.headline: A king who serves the field: farming, God, or Talmud?
5:8.body: Ibn Ezra says even a king depends on the field for his food. Rashi brings midrashim: God makes himself a worker for Zion, and a master of Bible and Mishnah must still serve the master of Talmud.

sources.quote: אפי׳ המלך שאין למעלה ממנו נעבד לשדה בעבור צרכו כי ממנו מחיתו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says even the king, with no one above him, serves the field for his needs, since his living comes from it.

sources.quote: הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא נַעֲשֶׂה פוֹעֵל לְצִיּוֹן
sources.says: Rashi says the King, God, becomes a worker for Zion, to avenge her and reward her builders.

sources.quote: מֶלֶךְ בְּמִקְרָא וּבְמִשְׁנָה עוֹדֶנּוּ צָרִיךְ לִהְיוֹת נֶעֱבָד לְבַעַל גְּמָרָא
sources.says: Rashi brings a reading that a 'king' of Bible and Mishnah still must serve the master of Talmud.

5:11.headline: Sweet sleep of the farmer, or of one who serves God?
5:11.body: Rashi and the Metzudat David say העבד is a farmer, who sleeps well whether he ate little or much. Rashi also brings a midrash: one who serves God, for few years or many, is rewarded alike, as Samuel's ten years leading Israel counted like Moses' forty.

sources.quote: עוֹבֵד הָאֲדָמָה יָשֵׁן, וְעָרְבָה שְׁנָתוֹ עָלָיו
sources.says: Rashi says the one who works the soil sleeps, and his sleep is sweet.

sources.quote: עובד האדמה הוא ישן וערבה שנתו עליו
sources.says: The Metzudat David says the farmer sleeps and his sleep is pleasant.

sources.quote: משֶׁה פִרְנֵס אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵל מ' שָׁנָה, וּשְׁמוּאֵל הַנָּבִיא פִרְנְסָם עֶשֶׂר שָׁנִים
sources.says: Rashi brings a midrash about one who serves God: Moses led Israel forty years and Samuel ten, and Scripture weighs them alike.

5:11.headline: The rich man can't sleep: too much wealth, or food?
5:11.body: Rashi and the Metzudat David say his many dealings keep him up at night thinking. Ibn Ezra also offers a bodily reading: a full stomach keeps him awake, as in Proverbs' warning about eating until you throw up.

sources.quote: וְשׂבַע נְכָסִים שֶׁל עָשִׁיר בַעַל פְּרַקְמַטְיָאוֹת הַרְבֵּה אֵינוֹ מַנִּיחַ לוֹ לִישׁוֹן
sources.says: Rashi says the plenty of a rich trader with many dealings does not let him sleep.

sources.quote: שביעת רוב העושר אין מניח לבעליו לישון
sources.says: The Metzudat David says a great surplus of wealth does not let its owner sleep.

sources.quote: או יהיה שבע שב אל המאכל כענין פן תשבענו והקאתו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says 'fullness' may refer to food, as in 'lest you be filled with it and vomit it'.

5:11.headline: A scholar who 'cannot sleep' even in the grave
5:11.body: Rashi brings a midrash that reads 'the rich man' as a scholar rich in teachings. He does not rest in the grave: whenever someone repeats a teaching in his name, his lips move there.

sources.quote: וְהַשָּׂבָע לֶעָשִׁיר. בַּעַל שְׁמוּעוֹת
sources.says: Rashi says the 'rich man' is a master of received teachings.

sources.quote: כָּל־תַּלְמִיד חָכָם שֶׁאוֹמְרִים דְּבַר שְׁמוּעָה מִפִּיו, שִׂפְתוֹתָיו דּוֹבְבוֹת בַּקָּבֶר
sources.says: Rashi says any scholar whose teaching is repeated in his name, his lips move in the grave.

5:12.headline: A 'sick evil': a painful one, or one that falls on you?
5:12.body: Ibn Ezra offers two roots: חלה, to be sick, so an evil like a bad illness; or חול, to whirl down, as a storm falls on the head of the wicked. The Metzudat David reads it as an evil that hurts very much.

sources.quote: יתכן היות חולה מן נחלה מכתי
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says חולה may come from 'my wound is sick', meaning an evil like a bad illness.

sources.quote: מן הפעלים שהעי״ן שלהם איננו שלם מן על ראש רשעים יחול
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it may instead come from the word in 'it will whirl down on the head of the wicked'.

sources.quote: נמצא רעה כאובה ביותר
sources.says: The Metzudat David says it is an evil that is very painful.

sources.quote: חולה. הוא מענין ולא חלו בה ידים
sources.says: Ralbag links the word to Lamentations' 'and no hands were laid on it'.

5:19.headline: God 'answers' his joy: testifies, provides, or keeps him busy?
5:19.body: Rashi and the Metzudat Zion read מענה from 'to testify': God is witness to the joy with which a person did good. Ibn Ezra reads it as 'provides', and Ralbag as 'keeps busy': God gives him things to do that make his heart glad.

sources.quote: הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עֵדוּת קְבוּעָה לָזֶה לְעוֹלָם
sources.says: Rashi says God is a lasting witness to this.

sources.quote: מענה. ענין עדות כמו לא תענה
sources.says: The Metzudat Zion says מענה means testimony, as in 'you shall not bear witness'.

sources.quote: כי האלהים מענה. ענינו ממציא כמו אענה את השמים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means God provides, as in 'I will answer the heavens'.

sources.quote: שה׳ יתברך נותן לו עסק וענין במה שישמח לבו
sources.says: Ralbag says God gives him business and occupation in what gladdens his heart.

6:1.headline: A common evil, or a heavy one?
6:1.body: Rashi reads ורבה as common: it happens to many people. Metzudat David and Ibn Ezra read it as great: it weighs heavily on a person.

sources.quote: בְּהַרְבֵּה בְּנֵי אָדָם הִיא נוֹהֶגֶת
sources.says: Rashi says this evil is found among many people.

sources.quote: הרעה הזאת היא גדולה על האדם ומצירה מאד
sources.says: Metzudat David says this evil is great for a person and hurts him badly.

sources.quote: רב בלשון הקדש על ארבעה ענינים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra lists four meanings of רב in Hebrew, and puts this verse under the meaning great.

6:2.headline: Wealth, or a wealth of Torah learning?
6:2.body: Plainly the verse speaks of money. Rashi also brings a midrash: wealth, property and honor stand for Scripture, Mishnah and Aggadah.

sources.quote: עשֶׁר וּנְכָסִים. לְפִי פְשׁוּטוֹ, כְּמַשְׁמָעוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says that by its plain sense it means what it says.

sources.quote: עשֶׁר וּנְכָסִים וְכָבוֹד. מִקְרָא, מִשְׁנָה וְאַגָּדָה
sources.says: Rashi says that in the midrash, wealth, property and honor are Scripture, Mishnah and Aggadah.

6:2.headline: A stranger enjoys it: an outsider, or a master of Talmud?
6:2.body: Plainly, a stranger who is not his heir ends up enjoying his money. In Rashi's midrash, the man knows Scripture and Mishnah but not Talmud, and the stranger who gains is the master of Talmud.

sources.quote: הזר ממנו שאינו ראוי לירשו הוא יאכל את העושר
sources.says: Metzudat David says a stranger, not fit to inherit him, will enjoy the wealth.

sources.quote: שֶׁלֹּא זָכָה לִגְמָרָא, וּמִתּוֹךְ כַּךְ, אֵין הֲנָאָה מִמֶּנּוּ בְּשׁוּם דְּבַר הוֹרָאָה
sources.says: Rashi, in the midrash, says the man never learned Talmud, so no one gains from him when a ruling is needed.

sources.quote: כִּי אִישׁ נָכְרִי יֹאכְלֶנּוּ. זֶה בַּעַל הַגְּמָרָא
sources.says: Rashi says the stranger is the master of Talmud.

6:3.headline: Great days, or enough of everything?
6:3.body: Rashi reads ורב as enough: his days had enough of every good thing. Metzudat Zion reads it as great: his days were full of honor.

sources.quote: וְרַב" לְשׁוֹן דַּי. דַּי לְכָל־טוֹבָה
sources.says: Rashi says ורב means enough: enough of every good.

sources.quote: ורב. גדול רוצה לומר מכובד
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means great, that is, honored.

6:3.headline: No burial: left for the dogs, or not even a shroud?
6:3.body: Rashi says such a man may be killed and eaten by dogs, as happened to Ahab. Ibn Ezra reads קבורה as the clothes the dead are buried in.

sources.quote: פְּעָמִים שֶׁנֶהֱרָג, וּכְלָבִים אוֹכְלִים אוֹתוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says sometimes he is killed and dogs eat him, as with Ahab.

sources.quote: וגם קבורה. התכריכין שיקבר בהם המת
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says קבורה here means the shrouds the dead are buried in.

sources.quote: וגם קבורה לא היתה לו מרוב הדלות והעוני
sources.says: Ralbag says he had no burial because he was so poor.

6:3.headline: Better off is the stillborn child
6:3.body: נפל is a child born dead. Rashi says it is better off because it came and went without seeing good, so it never longed for it and has nothing to grieve.

sources.quote: הנפל. כן יקרא הנולד מת
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says a child born dead is called נפל.

sources.quote: כִּי הַנֶּפֶל בַּהֶבֶל בָּא וְהָלַךְ, וְלֹא רָאָה טוֹבָה וְלֹא נִתְאַוָּה לָהּ, וְאֵין לוֹ לְהִצְטַעֵר
sources.says: Rashi says the stillborn came and went in emptiness, never saw good or wanted it, and has nothing to be sorry about.

6:6.headline: Two thousand years, or a thousand times a thousand?
6:6.body: Rashi and Metzudat David read it as a thousand years twice, two thousand years. Ibn Ezra reads it as a thousand times a thousand, a million years.

sources.quote: פעמים. שני פעמים אלף שהם שני אלפים
sources.says: Metzudat David says it is twice a thousand, two thousand.

sources.quote: וְאִם חָיָה אַלְפַּיִם שָׁנָה
sources.says: Rashi says it means if he lived two thousand years.

sources.quote: ואלף פעמים אלף אלפים כמו עשרים פעמים הם ארבע מאות
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says a thousand times means a thousand thousands, just as twenty times twenty is four hundred.

6:7.headline: The soul is not filled, or not cut off?
6:7.body: Ibn Ezra reads תמלא as filled: the soul is never satisfied. Metzudat Zion reads it as cut off, as in Job, and Metzudat David says giving charity keeps the soul from being cut off.

sources.quote: וענין וגם הנפש לא תמלא. שלא תשבע
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means the soul is never satisfied.

sources.quote: תמלא. ענינו כריתה וחתוך כמו התמלא בשכות עורו
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means cutting off, as in התמלא בשכות עורו in Job.

sources.quote: וגם הנפש. ישמור שלא תכרת, רוצה לומר שיתן מהונו צדקה לזכות את הנפש
sources.says: Metzudat David says a person should guard his soul from being cut off by giving charity from his wealth.

6:10.headline: Already named: past fame, or knowing what a thing is?
6:10.body: Rashi reads it as a man's past fame: his name was once great, but now it is known he was only human. Ralbag reads it as naming: a person can name the things whose nature he has grasped.

sources.quote: כְּבָר הָיָה וְעָבַר יָצָא לוֹ שֵׁם בִּשְׂרָרָה, וְעַתָּה חָלַף, וְנוֹדָע שֶׁהוּא אָדָם וְלֹא אֵל
sources.says: Rashi says he once had a name for power, but it has passed, and it is known he is a man and not a god.

sources.quote: ולזה יתואר האדם שהוא קורא שם לנמצאים שצייר מהותם ועצמותם
sources.says: Ralbag says a person is described as one who gives names to things whose nature he has grasped.

6:12.headline: Like a shadow: gone quickly, or never at rest?
6:12.body: Rashi says it is the shadow of a flying bird, gone in a moment, as David put it in Psalms. Metzudat David says a shadow never rests, so a person should keep doing good all his life.

sources.quote: כְּבָר פֵּרְשׁוֹ דָוִד אָבִיו, "יָמָיו כְּצֵל עוֹבֵר", זֶהוּ צִלּוֹ שֶׁל עוֹף הַפּוֹרֵחַ
sources.says: Rashi says David explained it in Psalms as a passing shadow, the shadow of a flying bird.

sources.quote: ולא ינוח כצל הזה אשר לא ינוח בעת מן העתים
sources.says: Metzudat David says a person should not rest, just as a shadow never rests at any time.

sources.quote: כמו שהצל איננו עומד רגע אחד כן ימיו ילכו ויעברו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says that just as a shadow does not stand still for a moment, so his days go and pass.

7:1.headline: Why a good name is compared to oil and not another drink
7:1.body: Rashi says oil is the right comparison because it floats: pour water into oil and it rises and shows, while other drinks soak the water up. Metzudat David says the scent of oil fades, while a good name keeps growing.

sources.quote: לְכַךְ הֻקַּשׁ שֵׁם טוֹב לְשֶׁמֶן יוֹתֵר מִשְּׁאָר מַשְׁקִין, שֶׁהַשֶּׁמֶן אַתָּה נוֹתֵן לְתוֹכוֹ מַיִם, וְהוּא צָף וְעוֹלֶה וְנִכָּר
sources.says: Rashi says a good name is compared to oil more than to other drinks because water poured into oil floats up and is seen.

sources.quote: כי שמן הטוב דרכו להפיג ריחו בכל עת והוא הולך וחסור, אבל שם טוב דרכו ללכת ולהתגבר בכל פעם
sources.says: Metzudat David says good oil loses its scent over time, but a good name keeps spreading and growing.

7:3.headline: 'Anger' may be God's frown, or a friend's open anger
7:3.body: Rashi reads כעס as a stern face from God: a rebuke would have served the generation of the Flood better than His laughter. Metzudat David reads it as a friend who shows anger, which is better than a smile that hides hatred.

sources.quote: טוֹב הָיָה לָהֶם לְדוֹר הַמַּבּוּל אִם הֶרְאָם הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא פָּנִים זְעוּמוֹת עַל עֲבֵרוֹת שֶׁבְּיָדָם
sources.says: Rashi says it would have been good for the generation of the Flood if God had shown them an angry face for their sins.

sources.quote: אבל אם מראה לו פנים שוחקות השנאה טמונה בלבו
sources.says: Metzudat David says that if a wronged friend shows a smiling face, the hatred stays hidden in his heart.

7:6.headline: The verse plays on סירים, thorns, and סיר, a pot
7:6.body: The image joins two words with the same letters and different meanings: thorns that crackle under a pot. Metzudat Zion calls it a play on the language, and Ibn Ezra calls it elegant speech, like the donkeys and cities in Judges.

sources.quote: כִּי כְקוֹל הַסִּירִים. עֲצֵי קוֹצִים
sources.says: Rashi says הסירים are thorn branches.

sources.quote: ואמר בלשון הנופל על הלשון
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the verse uses a phrase where one word falls on another, a play on words.

sources.quote: ובא סיר עם סירים ביחד ואינמו מענין אחד והוא לשון צחות
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says סיר and סירים come together though they do not mean the same, and calls it a language of elegance.

7:7.headline: 'Oppression' here may mean taunting and quarreling
7:7.body: עשק usually means oppression. Rashi and Metzudat Zion say it means quarrel and taunting: when a fool taunts a wise man, he confuses the wise man's mind.

sources.quote: עשֶׁק. לְשׁוֹן רִיב וְקִנְתּוּרִין
sources.says: Rashi says עשק is a word of quarrel and taunting.

sources.quote: כְּשֶׁהַכְּסִיל מְקַנְתֵּר אֶת הֶחָכָם, מְעַרְבֵּב דַּעְתּוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says that when a fool taunts the wise man, he confuses his mind.

sources.quote: העושק. ענין קנתור וערעור
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says העושק means taunting and challenge.

7:11.headline: Who are 'those who see the sun'?
7:11.body: Rashi says it means every living creature, and cites the Mishnah that a vow against 'those who see the sun' covers even the blind. Metzudat David says it means those who watch the heavens to draw luck from them.

sources.quote: הֵן כָּל הַבְּרִיּוֹת, כְּדִתְנַן: הַנּוֹדֵר מֵרוֹאֵי הַחַמָּה אָסוּר אַף בְּסוּמִין
sources.says: Rashi says it means all creatures, and cites the Mishnah that a vow against those who see the sun also binds the blind.

sources.quote: רואי השמש, רוצה לומר המסתכלים במערכת השמים
sources.says: Metzudat David says those who see the sun means those who study the order of the heavens.

7:13.headline: Who bent it: a man in his life, or God in creation?
7:13.body: עותו means bent or spoiled: Rashi says it is what a man twisted in his life, which no one can fix after death. Ralbag says it is what God left crooked in this low world, because its matter cannot take more good.

sources.quote: עותו. ענין קלקול
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says עותו means spoiling.

sources.quote: כִּי מִי יוּכַל לְתַקֵּן. לְאַחַר מִיתָה אֶת הַדָּבָר אֲשֶׁר עִוְּתוֹ בְחַיָּיו
sources.says: Rashi says no one can fix after death the thing he twisted in his life.

sources.quote: כי מי יוכל לתקן את אשר עותו ה׳ יתברך בזאת הבריאה השפלה מצד שלא יכול המקבל לקבל מהטוב שיעור יותר גדול
sources.says: Ralbag says it is what God left crooked in this low creation, since the receiver cannot take a greater measure of good.

7:14.headline: On a day of evil, 'see': study it, or watch from safety?
7:14.body: Metzudat David reads ראה as looking closely at the evil to learn why it came. Rashi reads it as watching evil fall on the wicked, so you are among those who see and not among those who are seen.

sources.quote: בעת בוא רעה בעולם הסתכל בהרעה להבין על מה באה
sources.says: Metzudat David says that when evil comes, look at it to understand why it came.

sources.quote: כְּשֶׁתָּבוֹא הָרָעָה עַל הָרְשָׁעִים, אַתָּה תִהְיֶה מִן הָרוֹאִים
sources.says: Rashi says that when evil comes on the wicked, you should be among the watchers.

7:16.headline: 'Don't be too righteous': three commentators, three examples
7:16.body: Rashi's example is Saul, who thought he was righteous and pitied the wicked. Metzudat David says it means forbidding yourself what the Torah allows, and Ibn Ezra says it means praying and fasting all day.

sources.quote: כְּשָׁאוּל, שֶׁדִּמָּה לִהְיוֹת צַדִּיק וְרִחֵם עַל הָרְשָׁעִים
sources.says: Rashi says it means like Saul, who imagined himself righteous and had mercy on the wicked.

sources.quote: לאסור על עצמך מה שהתירה התורה למען עשות סיג וגדר
sources.says: Metzudat David says it means forbidding yourself what the Torah permitted, to make a fence.

sources.quote: אם התפללת מן הבקר ועד הערב ותתענה והדומה להם
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means praying from morning to evening and fasting and the like.

7:16.headline: 'Be desolate' means turning away from settled life
7:16.body: Ibn Ezra says the warning is that you will turn away from the way of settled life, like hermits. He also records a view that the doubled ש stands for a dropped ת, so the full form would be תשתומם.

sources.quote: והענין תסור מדרך הישוב
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the meaning is that you will turn from the way of settled life.

sources.quote: יש אומרים כי דגשות השי"ן אינה לחסרון נו"ן נפעל רק לחסרון תי"ו התפעל והיה ראוי שיהיה תשתומם
sources.says: Ibn Ezra reports a view that the dagesh in the shin stands for a missing tav, so the form should be תשתומם.

7:17.headline: 'Do not be wicked' may mean 'do not panic'
7:17.body: Rashi reads תרשע as wickedness: even if you sinned a little, do not add to it. Metzudat Zion says it means alarm and confusion, and Metzudat David adds that you should not be so frightened that your mind is thrown off.

sources.quote: אֲפִלּוּ רָשַׁעְתָּ מְעַט, אַל תּוֹסִיף לְהַרְשִׁיעַ
sources.says: Rashi says that even if you sinned a little, do not add to it.

sources.quote: תרשע. ענין חרדה ובלבול כמו ובכל אשר יפנה ירשיע
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says תרשע means fear and confusion, as in 'wherever he turned he was thrown into confusion'.

sources.quote: אם בא לך דבר המחריד, אל תחרד יותר מדאי ולא תבלבל דעתך
sources.says: Metzudat David says that if something frightening comes, do not be too afraid or confuse your mind.

7:19.headline: 'Rulers' may be kings, or people who rule their own spirit
7:19.body: Rashi says the ten rulers are ten wicked kings who never repented. Metzudat David says they are rulers of the city, and Ralbag says they are people who rule over their own spirit.

sources.quote: וְטוֹב לוֹ מֵעֲשָׂרָה מְלָכִים שֶׁהִרְשִׁיעוּ וְלֹא שָׁבוּ מִדַּרְכָּם
sources.says: Rashi says it is better for him than ten kings who did wrong and did not turn back.

sources.quote: עשרה שליטים אשר היו בעיר למשול בה
sources.says: Metzudat David says the ten rulers were in the city to rule it.

sources.quote: החכמה תעוז לחכם מעשרה שליטים אשר היו בעיר והם המושלים ברוחם
sources.says: Ralbag says the rulers are those who rule over their own spirit.

7:19.headline: Why ten? A full count, ten named kings, or ten body parts?
7:19.body: Metzudat David and Ibn Ezra say ten is just a full count, the sum of the numbers. Rashi lists ten kings of Judah by name, and elsewhere reads the ten as the ten things in a person that make him guilty.

sources.quote: בעבור היותו סך חשבון
sources.says: Metzudat David says ten is used because it is the full sum of the count.

sources.quote: ומנין עשרה בעבור היותו סך חשבון והוא ראש הכלל
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says ten is used because it is the sum of the count, the head of the whole.

sources.quote: רְחַבְעָם, אֲבִיָּה, אֲחַזְיָה, יוֹאָשׁ אַחֲרֵי מוֹת יְהוֹיָדָע
sources.says: Rashi names the kings of Jerusalem, beginning Rehoboam, Abijah, Ahaziah, Joash.

sources.quote: אֵלּוּ עֲשָׂרָה דְבָרִים הַמְחַיְּבִים אֶת הָאָדָם
sources.says: Rashi gives another reading: these are the ten things that make a person liable.

7:25.headline: 'Reckoning': mathematics, thought, or the date of redemption?
7:25.body: Ralbag takes חשבון as the sciences of numbers and measures, and Metzudat Zion says it means thought, as in 9:10. Rashi reads it as working out the end of the exile.

sources.quote: וחשבון הם חכמות הלמודיות אשר יעיינו במספרים והשעורים
sources.says: Ralbag says חשבון means the mathematical sciences that study numbers and measures.

sources.quote: וחשבון. מלשון מחשבה וכן כי אין מעשה וחשבון
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says חשבון comes from the word for thought, as in 'there is no deed or reckoning'.

sources.quote: חָכְמַת פָּרָשַׁת פָּרָה אֲדֻמָּה וְחֶשְׁבּוֹן קֵץ הַגְּאֻלָּה
sources.says: Rashi says it means the wisdom of the red heifer and the reckoning of the end of the redemption.

7:26.headline: Here חרמים means 'nets', not 'things banned'
7:26.body: חרם often means a ban, but here Rashi, Metzudat Zion and Ibn Ezra say it is a net. Ibn Ezra adds that מצודים, the other word for snares, comes from ציד, hunting.

sources.quote: וַחֲרָמִים לִבָּהּ. לְשׁוֹן מִכְמֹרֶת, כְּמוֹ, יְגֹרֵהוּ בְחֶרְמוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says וחרמים is a word for a net, like 'he gathers it in his net'.

sources.quote: רשתות כמו יגורהו בחרמו
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says חרמים are nets, like 'he gathers it in his net'.

sources.quote: הוא מן ציד ומשקלו מרומים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says מצודים comes from ציד and has the form of מרומים.

sources.quote: וחרמים כענין רשת משטח חרמים כמוהו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says חרמים means a net, like the spreading of nets.

7:27.headline: 'Reckoning' may be a total, a comparison, or a chain of reasoning
7:27.body: Rashi says every good deed and every sin is counted one by one until they add up to a great sum. Metzudat David says it means setting a thing against its opposite, and Ibn Ezra says it means joining one claim to another to reach a third conclusion.

sources.quote: נִמְנִים לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא אַחַת אֶל אַחַת עַד שֶׁמִּצְטָרְפוֹת לְחֶשְׁבּוֹן גָּדוֹל
sources.says: Rashi says they are counted before God one by one until they add up to a great sum.

sources.quote: אין למצוא מחשבת בינה כי אם להעריך אחת אל אחת, רוצה לומר להעריך דבר אל הפכו
sources.says: Metzudat David says understanding comes only by comparing one thing to another, a thing against its opposite.

sources.quote: אז תוליד בין שתי המחברות דעת שלישית
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says that joining the two statements produces a third piece of knowledge.

7:29.headline: 'They' means Adam and Eve, once there were two
7:29.body: Rashi says the verse says 'they' because once Eve was joined to Adam, the one became two. Metzudat David says it means people in general, who seek many schemes.

sources.quote: מִּשֶּׁנִּזְדַּוְּגָה לוֹ חַוָּה אִשְׁתּוֹ וְנַעֲשׂוּ שְׁנַיִם וְנִקְרְאוּ הֵמָּה
sources.says: Rashi says that once Eve was joined to him and they became two, they were called 'they'.

sources.quote: והמה. בני אדם הם הם המבקשים מחשבות רבות
sources.says: Metzudat David says 'they' are people, the ones who seek many schemes.

8:1.headline: פשר, the Aramaic word Daniel uses for solving dreams
8:1.body: פשר means the meaning or solution of a thing. Ibn Ezra calls it an Aramaic word, and Rashi also hears in it making peace: Moses settled things between Israel and God.

sources.quote: ומלת פשר ממשפחת ארמית
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the word פשר belongs to the Aramaic family of words.

sources.quote: פשר. ענין פתרון ופירוש כמו מפשר חלמיין
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means solving and explaining, as in interpreting dreams in Daniel.

sources.quote: מי כמשה, עושה פשרים בין ישראל לאביהם שבשמים
sources.says: Rashi asks who is like Moses, who made settlements between Israel and their Father in heaven.

8:1.headline: Wisdom changes a face: it shines, or loses its hardness
8:1.body: ישנא means is changed. Rashi and Metzudat David say the wise man's face becomes unlike anyone else's, as with Moses' shining face; Ibn Ezra says the hardness leaves his face, because wisdom brings humility.

sources.quote: ועז פניו ישנא. משאר הבריות עד כי יראו
sources.says: Rashi says his face is different from other people's, until they fear to come near him, as with Moses.

sources.quote: חוזק מראית פניות נשתנה לשבח משאר בני האדם
sources.says: Metzudat David says the strength of his face is changed for the better from other people's.

sources.quote: סור עזות פנים ממנו כי החכמה תוליד הענוה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says boldness of face leaves him, because wisdom gives birth to humility.

8:2.headline: Keep the king's word: God's, or the ruler over you?
8:2.body: Rashi first reads the king as God, the King of the world. He then reads it as the foreign kings who rule Israel: obey them, as long as they do not make you break your oath to God.

sources.quote: אני צריך ונכון לשמר פי מלכו של עולם
sources.says: Rashi says I must keep the word of the King of the world.

sources.quote: דבר אחר: אני נכון לשמר פי מלכי האמות המושלים בנו
sources.says: Rashi gives a second reading: keep the word of the kings of the nations who rule over us.

sources.quote: ובלבד שלא יעבירנו את השבועה שנשבענו למקום
sources.says: Rashi adds: only as long as the king does not make us break the oath we swore to God.

8:5.headline: Is עת here "time" or "wisdom"?
8:5.body: Some read עת in this verse as wisdom, pointing to phrases like יודעי העתים, those who know the times. Ibn Ezra rejects this and shows that each of those verses is still about time.

sources.quote: יש מפרשים עת במקום הזה כמו חכמה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra reports that some explain עת here as wisdom.

sources.quote: וזה איננו נכון כי פירוש לעות את יעף לשום לו עת
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says this is not right, since the verse they cite means to set a time.

8:5.headline: משפט: God's punishment, or the custom of the land?
8:5.body: Rashi reads משפט as justice, the punishment that will reach the wicked in its time. Metzudat Zion reads it as custom, and Metzudat David says there are times to follow the king's rules, since the law of the land is law.

sources.quote: החכם יודע שיש עת קבוע לפקודת רשעים
sources.says: Rashi says the wise man knows there is a set time for the wicked to be punished.

sources.quote: ומשפט. ענין מנהג כמו ומשפט הכהנים
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says משפט means custom, as in the custom of the priests.

sources.quote: כי דינא דמלכותא דינא
sources.says: Metzudat David says the custom of the kingdom must be obeyed, since the law of the kingdom is law.

8:6.headline: רעת: a person's evil, or a person's thoughts?
8:6.body: רעת looks like the word for evil, and Rashi reads it that way: when a person's evil is full, punishment comes. Metzudat Zion reads it as thought, the same word as in Psalms, you understand my thought, בנתה לרעי.

sources.quote: כאשר רבה רעת האדם וסאתו גדושה, אז באה פקדתו
sources.says: Rashi says when a person's evil grows and his measure is full, then his punishment comes.

sources.quote: רעת. ענינו מחשבה כמו בנתה לרעי
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says רעת means thought, as in you understand my thought.

8:8.headline: רוח twice in one line: a will, then the breath of life
8:8.body: רוח appears twice in this verse. Rashi and Metzudat Zion read the first as will, since no one can rule over the will of God's messenger of death, and the second as the soul he comes to take.

sources.quote: ברוח. ברצון
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the first רוח means will.

sources.quote: הרוח. ענינו נשמת רוח האדם
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the second רוח means the human soul.

sources.quote: ברוחו ויצרו של שלוחו של מקום, לכלוא ולמנע ממנו את הרוח שבגופו
sources.says: Rashi says no one rules the will of God's messenger, to hold back from him the spirit in one's body.

8:8.headline: On the day he dies, David is no longer called king
8:8.body: No one has rule on the day of death. Rashi shows it from the Bible's own wording: elsewhere it says King David, but on the day he dies it says only that David's days drew near to die.

sources.quote: בכל מקום אתה מוצא "והמלך דוד", וביום מותו "ויקרבו ימי דוד למות", ולא הזכר המלכות כאן
sources.says: Rashi says everywhere we find King David, but on the day of his death it says David's days drew near to die, with no mention of kingship.

8:8.headline: No sending a substitute, or no weapon, in the war with death?
8:8.body: Rashi reads משלחת as sending: no one can say I will send my son or servant in my place. Metzudat Zion and Ralbag read it as a weapon, from שלח, a sword.

sources.quote: ואין משלחת במלחמה. זו לאמר: "אשלח בני או עבדי במקומי
sources.says: Rashi says it means one cannot say I will send my son or my servant in my place.

sources.quote: משלחת. ענינו נשק וכלי זיין כמו ויעש שלח לרוב
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says משלחת means weapons, as in he made many שלח.

sources.quote: משלחת. כמו שלח והוא החרב אשר יכו בה במלחמה
sources.says: Ralbag says it is like שלח, the sword used to strike in war.

8:10.headline: Buried, and they "came": back to power, or through their children?
8:10.body: The wicked were buried, and they came. Ibn Ezra says they came back into the world through their sons, who took their place; Metzudat David says the fallen wicked rose again, as if back from the grave.

sources.quote: ובאו לעולם שנית והענין שיבואו בניהם ויעמדו במקומם
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says they came into the world a second time, meaning their sons came and stood in their place.

sources.quote: ואחרים אמרו כי ובאו נעלמו כמו ובא השמש גם זה איננו נכון
sources.says: Ibn Ezra rejects reading came as vanished, like the sun going down.

sources.quote: ובאו. ואחר כך כאלו חזרו ובאו מקברם ושבו לקדמותן
sources.says: Metzudat David says afterward it was as if they came back from their graves and returned to their old standing.

8:10.headline: "Who did so" really means "who did right"
8:10.body: כן usually means so or thus. Metzudat Zion, Ibn Ezra and Ralbag read it here as right and true, as when God says the daughters of Zelophehad speak right, כן.

sources.quote: כן. ענינו אמת וראוי כמו כן בנות צלפחד דוברות
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says כן means true and fitting, as in the daughters of Zelophehad speak right.

sources.quote: והם אשר עשו כן האמת
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says they are the ones who did what is true.

sources.quote: אשר כן עשו. ר״ל אשר טוב עשו
sources.says: Ralbag says it means who did good.

8:12.headline: A sinner does evil "a hundred": a hundred what?
8:12.body: The verse just says a hundred and stops. Rashi fills in a hundred days, years or thousands; Metzudat David says harm to a hundred people; Ibn Ezra says a hundred times.

sources.quote: מאת. מקרא קצר, ודבוק לפניו, לומר מאת ימים, מאת שנים, מאת אלף
sources.says: Rashi says the verse is cut short and means a hundred days, a hundred years, or a hundred thousand.

sources.quote: אשר חוטא אחד שולט ועושה רע למאה אנשים
sources.says: Metzudat David says one sinner rules and does evil to a hundred people.

sources.quote: כי יראו חוטא אחד יעשה רע מאת פעמים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says people see one sinner do evil a hundred times.

8:15.headline: Eating and drinking in Ecclesiastes means Torah study, says a midrash
8:15.body: Plainly, Kohelet praises enjoying food and drink from what God gives. Rashi also brings a midrash: every time this book speaks of eating and drinking, it means the study of Torah.

sources.quote: ממה שחנן לו הקדוש ברוך הוא ולשמח בחלקו
sources.says: Rashi says it means eating from what God has given him and being happy with his share.

sources.quote: ומדרש אגדה: כל אכילה ושתיה שבקהלת אינה אלא תלמוד תורה
sources.says: Rashi brings a midrash that all eating and drinking in Ecclesiastes means Torah study.

8:16.headline: Whose eyes see no sleep: the greedy man's, or the author's?
8:16.body: The verse says his eyes see no sleep, but whose? Rashi says the wicked man chasing money and lust; Ibn Ezra and Metzudat David say it points back to my heart, so it is the author himself who cannot sleep.

sources.quote: שנה בעיניו איננו ראה. הרשע השטוף אחר הממון והעריות
sources.says: Rashi says it is the wicked man swept up in chasing money and forbidden relations who sees no sleep.

sources.quote: וי״ו עיניו שב אל לבי
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the his in his eyes goes back to my heart.

sources.quote: בעיניו איננו רואה. מוסב על הלב, רוצה לומר עיני ולבי
sources.says: Metzudat David says it refers back to the heart, meaning my eyes and my heart.

9:1.headline: Their servants, or their deeds?
9:1.body: עבדיהם looks like 'their servants', and Rashi reads it that way, as their students. Metzudat Zion and Ralbag read it as 'their deeds', as in Job 34:25.

sources.quote: הֵם תַּלְמִידֵיהֶם, מְשַׁמְּשֵׁיהֶם
sources.says: Rashi says these are their students, the people who serve them.

sources.quote: ועבדיהם. מעשיהם כמו לכן יכיר מעבדיהם
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means their deeds, as in Job, 'he knows their works'.

sources.quote: ועבדיהם. ר״ל ומעשיהם
sources.says: Ralbag says it means 'and their deeds'.

9:4.headline: 'Chooses' or 'is joined'? The same letters, reordered
9:4.body: It is written יבחר, 'chooses', but read יחבר, 'is joined': Rashi says whoever is joined to the living has hope, since he may repent. Ibn Ezra reads the written form: the dead can no longer choose.

sources.quote: אֲפִילּוּ הוּא רָשָׁע וְנִתְחַבֵּר לָרְשָׁעִים
sources.says: Rashi says that even a wicked person joined to the wicked has hope while he lives, since he may repent before he dies.

sources.quote: וכתוב יבחר וענינו המת לא יוכל לבחור
sources.says: Ibn Ezra notes the written form יבחר and says it means the dead cannot choose.
