9:4.headline: The living dog and the dead lion, named by Rashi
9:4.body: Rashi says the living dog is Nebuzaradan, a wicked servant who converted before he died. The dead lion is his master Nebuchadnezzar, whom a prophet called a lion, and who died in his wickedness.

sources.quote: טוֹב הָיָה לוֹ לִנְבוּזַרְאֲדָּן, שֶׁהָיָה עֶבֶד רָשָׁע וְנִתְגַּיֵּר
sources.says: Rashi says Nebuzaradan, a wicked servant who converted, was better off than his master Nebuchadnezzar, who is called a lion.

9:8.headline: White clothes: clean garments, or good deeds?
9:8.body: Metzudat David reads it plainly: wear clean clothes and enjoy life. Rashi reads the white clothes as good deeds kept ready at every hour, like a guest who does not know when the king will call him to the feast.

sources.quote: גם תתענג במלבוש נקי
sources.says: Metzudat David says it means to enjoy wearing clean clothes.

sources.quote: הַתְקֵן עַצְמְךָ בְכָל שָׁעָה בְמַעֲשֶׂה טוֹב, שֶׁאִם תָּמוּת הַיּוֹם, תִּכָּנֵס בְּשָׁלוֹם
sources.says: Rashi says to prepare yourself with good deeds at every hour, so that if you die today you go in peace, and gives the sages' parable of a king's feast.

sources.quote: כי המדות המגונות יוקשו לבגדים צואים והמדות היפות לבגדים לבנים
sources.says: Ralbag says bad traits are compared to dirty clothes and good traits to white clothes.

9:8.headline: Oil on your head: perfume, a good name, or wisdom?
9:8.body: Metzudat David reads it as real oil, for pleasure. Ibn Ezra reports an older reading that the oil is a good name, and Ralbag reads it as never letting up in the search for wisdom.

sources.quote: כי בכל עת תסוך ראשך בשמן למען התענג
sources.says: Metzudat David says it means to anoint your head with oil at all times, for pleasure.

sources.quote: וענין ושמן על ראשך אל יחסר שיהיה לו שם טוב
sources.says: Ibn Ezra reports that the early commentators read the oil as a good name, though he reads the passage as bodily pleasures.

sources.quote: וירצה בזה שלא יתעצל מהשגות המושכלות
sources.says: Ralbag says the oil means a person should not grow lazy in seeking knowledge.

9:10.headline: No 'reckoning' in the grave: judgment, planning, or mathematics?
9:10.body: Rashi gives two readings: the righteous face no reckoning there, or there is no more planning. Ralbag reads it as the study of numbers, one of the kinds of knowledge that end at death.

sources.quote: וְלֹא חֶשְׁבּוֹן לַצַּדִּיקִים כְּשֶׁיִּתְּנוּ הַחוֹטְאִים דִּין וְחֶשְׁבּוֹן
sources.says: Rashi says there is no reckoning for the righteous when sinners give account, and also that חשבון can mean thought or planning.

sources.quote: וחשבון. מחשבת בינה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means thinking with understanding.

sources.quote: לא בחשבון שהם חכמות הלמודיות
sources.says: Ralbag says חשבון here means the mathematical sciences.

9:10.headline: Here שאול is simply the grave
9:10.body: Ibn Ezra says שאול in this verse is the grave, not a place only for the wicked. His proof is that Jacob, a righteous man, says he will go down to שאול mourning his son.

sources.quote: בשאול שהוא הקבר כי ימצא שאול לצדיקים עמו כי ארד אל בני אבל שאולה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says שאול is the grave, since the righteous go there too, as Jacob said, 'I will go down to my son in mourning to שאול'.

sources.quote: בשאול. בקבר
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means in the grave.

9:11.headline: פגע: a deadly blow, a prayer, or a meeting of stars
9:11.body: Metzudat Zion reads פגע as a blow that kills. Rashi also reads it as pleading in prayer, and Ibn Ezra as a meeting of heavenly bodies.

sources.quote: ענינו מכת מות כמו גש פגע בו
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means a death blow, as in 'go, strike him down'.

sources.quote: וְהַפְּגִיעָה וְהַתְּחִנָּה יִהְיוּ רְגִילִין בָּהֶם
sources.says: Rashi says it can be read plainly, or as pleading and prayer, which should be a regular habit for them.

sources.quote: ופירוש פגע פגיעת אחד מן המערכת באחד מהשבעה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says פגע is the meeting of one heavenly body with one of the seven planets.

9:12.headline: An 'evil' net here means a poor, weak one
9:12.body: רעה usually means evil, but Rashi reads it as a poor, weak net that still catches big fish. Metzudat Zion reads it as a net that hurts.

sources.quote: כְּדָגִים גְּדוֹלִים שֶׁנֶּאֱחָזִים בִּמְצוֹדָה גְרוּעָה וַחֲלוּשָׁה
sources.says: Rashi says it means big fish caught in a poor, weak net, and cites the sages that it is a hook no bigger than a needle.

sources.quote: רעה. רוצה לומר מכאיבה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says רעה means painful.

9:14.headline: The small city is a person's body
9:14.body: The sages read this story as a picture of a person: the small city is the body, the great king the evil inclination, and the poor wise man the good one. Ibn Ezra knows this reading but says the story means what it says.

sources.quote: וּמִדְרַשׁ אַגָּדָה: עִיר קְטַנָּה. זֶה הַגּוּף
sources.says: Rashi cites the midrash that the small city is the body.

sources.quote: זֶה יֵצֶר הָרַע, שֶׁכָּל אֵבָרָיו מַרְגִּישִׁים בּוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says the great king is the evil inclination, which all the limbs feel.

sources.quote: נקרא יצר רע "מֶלֶךְ גָּדוֹל" (קהלת ט,יד)
sources.says: The Guide cites the sages that the evil inclination is called the 'great king' of this verse, in a parable about the body and its powers.

sources.quote: והנכון שאינו מדבר על דרך משל כי אם כמשמעו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra reports the reading of the city as the body, but says the correct view is that it is not a parable.

9:15.headline: No one 'remembered' him: in the mind, or in speech?
9:15.body: Ibn Ezra says זכר can mean remembering in the heart or mentioning with the mouth. Here he reads it as speech: before the poor man saved the city, nobody even spoke of him.

sources.quote: ויותר נכון הוא בעיני להיות מלת זכירה פעם בלב ופעם בפה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says זכירה sometimes means in the heart and sometimes in the mouth, and here no one in the city mentioned the wise man before he saved them.

sources.quote: כי היה נבזה בעיני כל ולא עלה זכרונו בפי אנשים
sources.says: Metzudat David says he was despised by all and his name never came up in people's mouths.
